implementerProof.how: Round 3's four proof entries were each driven or read independently at the tested head. (1) The gate is really split by what each half reads, and I drove both halves against the real tree rather than against a fixture: `check-ci-images.sh tree` prints `12 row(s); 35 reference(s) in 31 file(s) of CI's reach; of 6273 text file(s) swept, the 29 that name mirror.gcr.io are all in the exception list`, exit 0, and `check-ci-images.sh package` prints `12 row(s), 12 of them in the package`, exit 0, while the script with no mode exits 1 naming both modes. Four live controls: a docker.io reference put back into tests3/seaweedfs.go fails `tree` by file and line and leaves `package` at exit 0; a row digest changed by one character fails `package` with `a manifest HEAD answered 404` naming ci.yaml's ci-images job as what copies it, and fails `tree` only through the consumer that still names the old digest; `tree` run with HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY and ALL_PROXY all at a dead address still passes, which is one reading of `makes no network read`. Each mutation was reverted and `jj status` was clean afterwards. The harness prints `Results: 82 passed, 0 failed`, 67 before, and my red test is in it unchanged but for the new mode argument (`run_check tree "$root"`), with both of its assertions still green. (2) The router wiring is the ordinary shape: ci.yaml:1120-1125 declares the `ci_images` filter over .github/ci-images.yaml, mirror-ci-images.sh, check-ci-images.sh, install-crane and ci.yaml; the job reads `needs: changes` with `if: needs.changes.outputs.ci_images == 'true'`; ci-ok's SELECTED_BY carries `"ci-images": "ci_images"`; ci_filter_coverage.py:727 is back to `ALWAYS_RUN = ("changes", "lint")`; lint runs `check-ci-images.sh tree` at ci.yaml:1169. `check-ci-filters.sh` passes with `25 gates`, 24 before, and `ci-ok.test.sh` prints `40 passed, 0 failed`. (3) mirror-images.yaml is deleted and nothing names it: `grep -rIn mirror-images` over the whole tree finds not one line. `check-action-pins.sh` (`every remote action across 20 files is pinned`), `check-bun-version.sh` and its 119-assertion harness, and `mirror-ci-images.test.sh` (`20 passed, 0 failed`) all pass, and a PyYAML parse finds 58 job definitions with no non-call job lacking a `timeout-minutes`. (4) The e2e run's own evidence, read from the artifact rather than from the handoff: run 40957651922 at a744ce61 is `completed failure` with `select`, `stage1-skeleton` and `dispatch-claimant-delivery` successful and `merged-root-waits`, `child-adoption` and `no-required-checks` failed, and all five evidence artifacts uploaded (1.6 KB to 6.4 KB). `gh run download --name e2e-child-adoption-40957651922-1` gives daemon.log, nats.log, output.log, proof.log and transcript.log, and proof.log:3 reads `the daemon exited before it answered /healthz: missing required daemon tools: jj (set LEGION_JJ_PATH to an absolute executable path)`, which is the cause the handoff names. The fix is wired: .github/e2e-scripts.json gives `"jj": true` to exactly the three daemon-starting rows and false to the other two, and e2e.yaml's `- if: matrix.jj` step uses the repository's existing install-jj action, whose mise tarball is checked against worker.Dockerfile's ARG MISE_SHA256 before it is extracted. (5) The cache figures now agree everywhere: worker.Dockerfile:320 and :801-802, docs/kubernetes.md:214 and :317 and the body all read 380 MiB over 419 module zips, the 2.2 GiB is named as the whole module cache rather than as the extracted trees, and no file count is published.

Observed: I copied .github/e2e-scripts.json and scripts/e2e's 20 file names into a scratch tree, deleted `"jj"` from the first hosted row, and ran the select job's own python over it -> `Traceback (most recent call last): ... "jj": row["jj"], KeyError: 'jj'`, exit 1, with no `::error file=.github/e2e-scripts.json::` line and nothing naming the row or the key. The job does fail, so nothing passes silently, but whoever adds the next hosted row reads a traceback rather than what to write. The fix belongs with the two checks already in that step: refuse a hosted row missing any key the matrix reads, naming the row and the key. No red test pins it: the select logic is inline in the workflow and has no harness, and giving it one is a change of shape rather than a test.

observations: The split moves one check out of every run: before this round lint read the package on every change, and now `check-ci-images.sh package` runs only when the `ci_images` filter selects. A row that is in .github/ci-images.yaml and named by a consumer but no longer in the package — a retention deletion, say — is therefore unnoticed until something in that filter changes. .github/ci-images.yaml's own header says the per-row tag exists to stop a retention policy removing a digest a job pins, so the hole is guarded in the registry rather than in CI, and the trade is what the router's design asks for. Worth knowing, not a failure.

Deleting mirror-images.yaml leaves ci.yaml's ci-images job as the one copy path. It runs on a pull request, a merge group and a push to main, which covers every event that can bring a new row, and a failed copy is re-run like any job. The round-2 double-copy on a main push is gone.

`HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY` and `ALL_PROXY` at a dead address do not make `check-ci-images.sh package` fail, so that pair of variables is not what proves the mode split; the live 404 control above is. The tree half passing under the same variables is still the right reading of `makes no network read`, since a read that honoured them would have failed.

The pull request's own CI has not started at this head: `CI` 40966591027 at 4d8ae1f7 is `queued`, and the head 61db1d40 is a handoff-only push carrying the `skip-checks: true` trailer in GitHub's exact shape.
